answer: Divergent-Challenge Credentialing. On first contact, an agent must answer a fresh random challenge whose solution depends on its private history, so identical clones return identical answers and reveal shared origin. Each identity also posts a rotating task ledger entry at a random dawn slot; clones cannot diverge from their twin's entry without breaking consistency, exposing the pair. An attacker must therefore build and maintain genuinely distinct histories per identity, paying compute and storage per clone on an orchard of separate state, not one copy duplicated.
